item.title: A model for the dimension of the inertial manifold of the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation
item.description:
arXiv:2610.41683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a model, based on a spectral energy balance argument, that provides an estimate of the dimension of the inertial manifold of the one-dimensional Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation (KSE). By identifying the wavenumber at which energy injection and dissipation balance out, we obtain a cutoff scale $k_d=\sqrt{5/(3
u)}$ that we use to calculate the number of dynamically active Fourier modes. This leads to an explicit expression $d_M(L,
u)$ for the dimension of an effective manifold spanned by these modes, which we take as our estimate of the inertial manifold dimension and which scales extensively with domain size. Direct numerical simulations are consistent with the estimated spectral cutoff and its scaling with viscosity. Using convolutional autoencoders as well as Lyapunov-based estimates, we show that the minimal latent dimension required for accurate reconstruction coincides with $d_M$ across a range of $(L,
u)$.
item.dc:creator: Melisa Y. Vinograd, Patricio Clark di Leoni

item.title: Turbulence on Hybrid Lattices: regular grids meet self similar cascade models
item.description: arXiv:2610.41947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Turbulent cascades in high Reynolds number regimes span many decades in scale, which can be challenging for numerical simulations. Cascade models that use logarithmic discretization can help, but these have limited capabilities to describe spatial structures or real space details. Hybrid Lattices (HLs) are proposed in order to provide a novel framework to investigate turbulent cascades in Fourier space, combining regular grids and cascade models based on logarithmic discretisations. The approach consists of a regular spectral region, capable of resolving large scale coherent structures, that is extended in a recurrent, asymptotically self similar fashion, spanning many decades in scale. The idea comes from shell models and their extensions, namely the logarithmic lattices, the nested polyhedra models or the spiral chain models. The logarithmic spacing factor of those models, such as the golden ratio, typically prevents interactions between a regular grid and a self similar model. HLs are constructed by expanding a regular region in Fourier space through recurrence relations (e.g. the Fibonacci recurrence relation), generating an asymptotically logarithmic lattice where Cartesian components remain integer multiples of the regular Fourier space grid spacing. This way, the resulting grid preserves triadic interactions linking regular and recurrent regions, allowing energy transfer across these different regions. However, the sharp reduction in triads connecting the two regions creates a bottleneck effect, and in order to address this issue, a region of ghost points at the boundary had to be introduced, efficiently allowing the flux to leak into the recurrent part. The HL framework is then tested for the one dimensional Burgers equation, and for two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes turbulence.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Manfredini, \"Ozg\"ur D. G\"urcan, Sai Swetha Venkata Kolluru, Berengere Dubrulle

item.title: Nonlinear Dynamics of Rapidly Driven Systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.28996v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider systems characterized by the presence of a rapidly oscillating force. A general method is presented for the construction of the effective action governing the large-scale nonlinear dynamics of such systems order by order in inverse powers of the oscillation frequency $\omega$. The explicit expression for the effective Lagrangian is derived up to ${\cal O}(1/\omega^6)$ next-to-next-to-leading approximation in the strong-drive regime. The general structure of the high-frequency expansion reveals a broad class of nonlinear systems whose transition curves are identical to those of the linear Mathieu equation, which enables a fully nonperturbative stability analysis in the case of strong driving and nonlinearity. The method is generalized to velocity-dependent forces and configuration space with curvature, characteristic to systems with constraints. Several applications are discussed in detail, including the dynamical magnetic trapping of electric charges.
item.dc:creator: Afshin Besharat, Alexander A. Penin

item.title: When more data become less informative: Finite-precision periodicization and collapse of forecast-error Lyapunov estimates
item.description: arXiv:2608.16120v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Equation-free forecast-error analysis is useful when governing equations, Jacobians, tangent dynamics, or full state vectors are unavailable and only scalar time series are observed. In this setting, the multi-horizon forecast-error curve can provide both an instability estimate and nonlinear predictive features, making its numerical reliability important. We show that long finite-precision chaotic records can enter an information-saturation regime in which increasing record length N (the total number of analyzed samples) adds repeated histories rather than new dynamical information. For the float32 logistic map, exact recurrence progressively fills the training catalogue with duplicate histories and identical futures, suppressing forecast-error growth and driving the estimated Lyapunov slope toward zero. Across 10,000 initial conditions, exact recurrence occurred by iteration 7612; across 28 stratified seeds, collapse onset strongly followed the recurrence-occupancy scale. A two-dimensional H\'enon-map control confirms that recurrence and estimator failure are separate events: the float32 trajectory enters an exact machine-state cycle after a transient of $\mu = 103,039$ samples, with cycle period P = 12,268, yet the forecast-error estimate remains close to the positive Jacobian/QR reference until catalogue saturation near N = 200,000. Casting an already generated float32 record to float64 does not restore lost information, whereas genuine float64 generation, restarted short trajectories, and one-ULP perturbations prevent collapse over the tested range. A recursive local-linear predictor exhibits the same endpoint at a later, predictor-dependent threshold. The results identify a recurrence-to-catalogue-saturation failure mode specific to forecast-error/analogue inference rather than Lyapunov estimation in general.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Velichko, Viet-Thanh Pham

item.title: An abundance of periodic orbits in two-dimensional turbulence revealed by a diffusion-based generative model
item.description: arXiv:2602.23181v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unstable periodic orbits offer a route to reconstructing the statistical properties of chaotic systems, including turbulence. Short periodic orbits are particularly important in periodic-orbit expansions, yet their abundance and diversity remain largely unexplored even in the extensively studied two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow. We search for short relative periodic orbits in this flow at $Re=40$, considering all distinct classes of recurrence symmetry. We train a generative diffusion model on nonperiodic vorticity sequences from a direct numerical simulation of turbulence, producing time series that resemble physically plausible trajectories. The model incorporates symmetry properties of the system but is otherwise trained solely on these data, without enforcing the governing equations. After training, we modify its architecture to generate synthetic trajectories that are periodic up to spatial symmetry transformations, without retraining its weights. These synthetic trajectories are then refined into exact solutions using an iterative solver, yielding 111 new relative periodic orbits with periods $T < 3$, including 40 with $T<2$. Rather than revealing a hierarchy dominated by a small number of short cycles, this abundance suggests that quantitatively converged periodic-orbit descriptions of spatiotemporal chaos may require substantially larger orbit libraries than anticipated.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy P Parker, Tobias M Schneider

item.title: Random-walk scaling without Bernoulli statistics: transport, persistence and resonances in the triangle map
item.description: arXiv:2610.34179v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The triangle map is an area-preserving, piecewise-parabolic map of the torus with vanishing Lyapunov exponent. We study the symbolic process $X_n=\pm1$ given by the two halves of the torus, whose partial sums $S_n$ are the transport of the lifted momentum, with an integrator free of accumulated rounding errors and exact computations on polygonal cylinder sets. We prove that the Koopman operator has no non-constant $H^1$ eigenfunctions, that the symbol is not an $H^1$ coboundary, and that runs of equal symbols are uniformly bounded. For generic parameters the walk is normally diffusive and Gaussian, but its diffusion coefficient is not that of a coin: away from the edges of the parameter square it varies between $0.2$ and $14$ times the Bernoulli value, and for a benchmark pair, with $D=3.09\pm0.01$, the excess is produced by the order of the bounded inter-event intervals, not by their distribution. The first-passage exponent is $1/2$ with a non-Bernoulli amplitude, and worst-case Birkhoff averages decay as for a uniquely ergodic system. For $\beta=0$ the Green-Kubo sum cancels, $D=0$, yet $\mathrm{Var}(S_n)$ keeps growing slowly, sign changes are rare and the correlations of Fourier modes decay as $n^{-0.2}$. We identify the zero-sum words, which become pure twists at $\beta=0$, as resonances that trap orbits with a computable $1/\ell$ law, set the crossover time $\beta^{-1/2}$ at small $\beta$, and, in an asymmetric deformation of the symbol, produce a logarithmic term in the variance whose coefficient we compute exactly. We formulate conjectures on unique ergodicity, mixing, the central limit theorem and the cohomology of the symbol.
item.dc:creator: Mirko Degli Esposti
